# Preface {.unnumbered}

**This is a publishing scaffold, not a published or accepted engineering textbook.**

The intended book develops first-principles coherent receiver theory and practical design methods for experienced RF engineers. Its provisional chapter organization is recorded in the accepted planning package under ADR-0004; technical development remains subject to review.

The opening technical unit develops physical representations and conversion signs
through a continuous two-channel phase comparison. It is a provisional draft,
not the complete planned Chapter 1.

The next bounded teaching units develop scalar stochastic phase reasoning,
observation-weighted coherence, and covariance/quadratic forms. They connect
dependence and circular quantities to finite observation and coupled error models.
Phase/delay inference then separates local precision from ambiguity; model
adequacy tests sensitivity and numerical reasoning before acquisition/tracking
examines wanted-signal retention. These developing foundations retain provisional
status and do not complete their planned chapters.

[Fields, geometry and physical transduction](fields-geometry-transduction.qmd)
then connects incident fields to loaded receiver voltages and shows what electronic
injection cannot establish. [Physical disturbances](physical-disturbance-paths.qmd)
constructs noise and interference from sources and their actual transfer paths.
[Extraction, integration and rejection](extraction-integration-rejection.qmd)
uses those responses and disturbances to calculate detection outcomes and retained
wanted information. Each bounded unit includes a worked receiver decision, a
misleading alternative and a changed-assumption exercise. Their diagrams and
calculations describe supplied models; they do not establish hardware behavior
or complete the planned chapters.

The opening requirement framing now leads to an exercised
[frequency, phase and delay plan](frequency-phase-delay-transfer.qmd), with
conversion orientation, unwanted bands and state-sensitive references. The
[architecture and allocation treatment](feasibility-architecture-allocations.qmd)
then intersects headroom, information, time and resource limits before refining
them through physically constructed correlations and environmental paths.
A model can reject a proposed operating point or expose a missing interface;
passing its equations does not demonstrate a realizable receiver.

The developed canonical reading path currently ends at Chapter 12. The publishing
demonstration and relative-phase pilot are grouped as **development supplements**;
their temporary rendered chapter numbers are outside the accepted canonical
sequence. Canonical Chapter 13, on calibration observability and operational
metrology, is not supplied by those supplements.

The publishing demonstration tests mathematics, references, SVG figures and bibliography wiring. The following dual-channel relative-phase pilot develops a bounded illustrative engineering argument and supporting calculations. It has no hardware measurements, specialist acceptance or actual reader-trial evidence.
